content: HEY2, also referred to as Hairy/enhancer-of-split related with YRPW motif protein 2 or cardiovascular helix-loop-helix factor 1 (CHF1), is a protein encoded by the HEY2 gene in humans. CHF1 belongs to the hairy and enhancer of split-related (HESR) family of transcription factors, which are characterized by a basic helix-loop-helix (bHLH) structure. The protein encoded by this gene can form either homodimers or heterodimers, which are localized to the nucleus. Within the nucleus, these dimers interact with a histone deacetylase complex to suppress the transcription of target genes. The expression of HEY2 is regulated by the Notch signaling pathway. In mice, two genes that are similar to HEY2 and function redundantly are essential for proper embryonic cardiovascular development. These genes are also involved in the processes of neurogenesis and somitogenesis. Additionally, alternative splicing of HEY2 transcripts has been observed, but the biological significance of these spliced variants remains unclear. From a clinical perspective, common genetic variants in HEY2, as well as in the SCN5A and SCN10A genes, have been linked to Brugada syndrome, a cardiac condition associated with an increased risk of sudden cardiac death. HEY2 has been demonstrated to interact with specific proteins, including Sirtuin 1 (SIRT1) and Nuclear receptor co-repressor 1 (NCOR1). These interactions likely contribute to its role in transcriptional repression and other cellular processes.
